issues.failure_explanation: For x in C_q^j, the image Psi_q(x) ranges over an interval of length about |lambda|_1(h-delta^mu) around a_q^j. The spacing of neighbouring images along a row is only lambda_p h, which is much smaller for Sprecher-like lambda (lambda_1/lambda_2<h~). So Psi_q(x) can lie beyond the neighbouring node or closer to the image of a different cube. The proof then needs g_q(Psi_q(x)) in [b_q^j+-|s_{k+1}-s_k|], with node k belonging to the cube containing x (or the Euclidean-nearest cube in a gap). Neither follows from the argmin rule, which minimizes image distance, not Euclidean distance. Remark remk-Slides asserts without proof that the head/tail dislocation intervals are never hit. But Psi_q is onto [0,|lambda|_1], so those values are attained.

The construction selects the interpolation row from x via the argmin/sigma* rule, so the value assigned depends on x and the row, not only on t=Psi_q(x).
